taxonomic_note: Current Kew/POWO accepts Ludwigia octovalvis; Central Texas material is commonly treated as subsp. octovalvis, also accepted by Kew.
look_here_first: Locate several stem nodes: leaves alternate, typically narrow and softly hairy on upright branched shoreline shoots. At flowering, see a showy four-petaled yellow corolla and the conspicuously long inferior ovary BELOW the sepals; usually eight stamens. Compare L. repens opposite nodes and tiny four-stamen flowers.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays — UT Plant Resources Center Purola Preserve flora lists Ludwigia octovalvis as naturally occurring. Travis — UT PRC Travis County Onagraceae index includes Ludwigia octovalvis. Williamson — UT PRC provides a detailed Ludwigia octovalvis subsp. octovalvis treatment.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Subspecies records are reconciled to the accepted species concept without inventing additional counties.

best_field_traits: alternate narrow leaves up upright branched stem
large four-petaled yellow flower with eight stamens
long inferior ovary / elongated seed capsule
local stems usually five-ridged; confirm rather than assume
morphology_keys.stem: Local Williamson County specimens have strongly five-ridged, usually hairy stems; Flora of North America allows terete or ridged stems across the species.
morphology_keys.flower: Usually four broad showy yellow petals; locally around 23–39 mm across and commonly eight stamens in two sets (rarely five sepals/petals and ten stamens).
morphology_keys.ovary: Inferior, distinctly elongated and often low eight-ribbed on four-sided base; distinguish from Ludwigia repens very short four-angled inferior ovary.
morphology_keys.fruit: Long narrow cylindrical to club-shaped many-seeded capsule, 38–45 mm in Williamson specimens; local plants typically show 8 valve splits, but FNA describes 4–8 valves across broader species.
morphology_keys.joey_field_note: Joey explicitly uses this plant to teach an inferior ovary, showing the ovary below the visible flower parts at close range.
morphology_keys.habit: Erect, much-branched, often taprooted wetland herb/subshrub, usually growing on moist shorelines; forms can vary.
morphology_keys.leaf_arrangement: Alternate helically, one leaf per successive node; contrast the opposite pairs of Ludwigia repens.
morphology_keys.leaves: Usually narrow oblanceolate to oblong-lanceolate, mostly entire, with very short petioles; often short hairy and not glossy.

comparisons.key_distinctions: L. octovalvis: alternate narrow usually hairy leaves on erect branched shoreline stems, large 8-stamen yellow flowers and an elongated ovary/capsule. L. repens: opposite leaves on creeping node-rooting stems, about 6 mm yellow 4-stamen flowers and short bell-shaped fruits.

diagnostic_comparison.look_first: Alternate narrow leaves on upright stems vs opposite paired leaves on creeping stem.
diagnostic_comparison.strong_reproductive_split: Octovalvis ca. 23–39 mm corolla and typically eight stamens; repens ca. 6 mm flower and four stamens.
diagnostic_comparison.strong_fruit_split: Octovalvis narrow capsule often 38–45 mm long in Williamson vs repens bell-shaped capsule 6–7.5 mm long.
diagnostic_comparison.caution: These lengths describe Williamson County specimens; field dimensions can vary. Five stem ridges are characteristic of locally described material but not universal.
